bibliography.abstract: TOM-GS represents editable video with static spatial Gaussians and continuous time-varying opacity.

scope.rationale: Each Gaussian receives an explicit continuous temporal support through its learnable opacity mean and scale.

method.problem: Dynamic video representations based on complex spatial deformation are difficult to edit with conventional 3D tools.
method.solution: Keep Gaussian geometry static and express temporal change only through a continuous learnable opacity envelope for each primitive.

components.name: Static Gaussian geometry
components.role: Keeps spatial components compatible with standard Gaussian editing operations.

components.name: Temporal opacity
components.role: Assigns each Gaussian a learnable temporal mean and scale so it fades smoothly into and out of the video.

components.name: Pose initialization
components.role: Uses robust off-the-shelf pose estimates to ground the static spatial representation.

algorithm_steps: Initialize static spatial Gaussians from posed video, learn their appearance and temporal opacity envelopes, then edit the static geometry with standard tools.
assumptions: Off-the-shelf camera pose estimates are sufficiently robust for the input video.
limitations: The abstract does not report how topology changes or severe pose errors affect the static geometry assumption.

methodology.summary: Evaluates video fidelity and compatibility with manual and physics-based editing.

evidence.excerpt: We introduce TOM-GS, an editable video representation that forgoes complex deformations in favor of regular 3D Gaussians.

bibliography.abstract: DynHair learns explicit strand-level hair dynamics inside a Gaussian head avatar from synchronized video.

scope.rationale: The method tracks and deforms structured Gaussian hair strands over time as part of an animatable head avatar.

method.problem: Hair motion depends on inertial history and gravity, so pose-conditioned static or instantaneous avatar deformation produces rigid or blurry hair.
method.solution: Represent hair as explicit Gaussian strands and predict history-dependent strand displacements from head kinematics and gravity while jointly optimizing the Gaussian head appearance.

components.name: Hybrid avatar
components.role: Combines explicit structured hair strands with unstructured face and upper-body Gaussians.

components.name: Hair dynamics network
components.role: Encodes motion history with an LSTM and applies FiLM-conditioned per-strand deformation.

components.name: Physics supervision
components.role: Regularizes learned hair motion together with photometric and geometric objectives.

algorithm_steps: Initialize canonical hair strands and head Gaussians, encode head-motion history, predict strand displacements, jointly optimize motion and appearance, and composite both Gaussian components.
assumptions: The primary setup uses synchronized multi-view video and tracked head motion.
limitations: Untracked shoulder motion can blur the shoulder region during cross-reenactment.

setup.summary: Uses synchronized captures and evaluates self-reenactment, cross-reenactment, and hair editing.

optimization.summary: Jointly optimizes hair motion and appearance with the Gaussian face and upper-body representation.

methodology.summary: Compares hair dynamics and temporal consistency in self- and cross-reenactment and evaluates new synchronized captures.

ablations.finding: Motion history, acceleration, relative gravity, and the learned deformer each improve motion realism or temporal stability.

evidence.locator: DynHair project: main idea and ablations
evidence.excerpt: Hair strands are initialized using Im2Haircut prior model, and the upper body is represented with unstructured 3D Gaussians.
The repository currently contains only README, license, and ignore files; the declared license is MIT.

bibliography.venue: Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers 2026
bibliography.abstract: SplatStream provides fine-grained scalable coding and adaptive delivery for dynamic Gaussian scenes.

scope.rationale: The system compresses, packetizes, predicts, and streams time-varying Gaussian scene representations.

method.problem: Large dynamic Gaussian representations and frame redundancy make bandwidth-adaptive low-latency delivery difficult.
method.solution: Layer Gaussian quality and resolution, predict across layers and time, prioritize important primitives, and expose the layers through MPEG-DASH.

components.name: Scalable layers
components.role: Separate Gaussian content into quality and spatial-resolution refinements.

components.name: Cross-layer predictor
components.role: Uses a lightweight transformer for inter-layer and temporal B-frame prediction.

components.name: Importance packetizer
components.role: Orders Gaussian packets using a volume-opacity importance measure.

algorithm_steps: Create base and enhancement layers, predict residual content across layers and frames, packetize by visual importance, and map packets to DASH sub-representations.
assumptions: The input is a dynamic Gaussian sequence suitable for layered predictive coding.
limitations: Codec implementation details and network adaptation experiments require full-source review.

methodology.summary: Evaluates adaptive, progressive, low-latency delivery under changing bandwidth.

evidence.excerpt: This paper presents SplatStream, a fine granular scalable Gaussian splatting framework for dynamic 3D scene delivery.

bibliography.abstract: StructureGS reconstructs articulated objects by constraining Gaussian parts with explicit object structure.

scope.rationale: The method represents multiple movable object parts with Gaussian primitives and reconstructs their articulated configurations.

method.problem: Photometric supervision alone entangles geometry, appearance, and articulation, producing weak part boundaries and structural artifacts.
method.solution: Use oriented part boxes to impose spatial coherence within parts and contact connectivity between adjacent articulated parts.

components.name: Part boxes
components.role: Provide explicit oriented spatial support for each articulated component.

components.name: Spatial-coherence loss
components.role: Keeps each Gaussian part compact inside its designated structural region.

components.name: Connectivity loss
components.role: Preserves physically plausible contacts between neighboring movable parts.

algorithm_steps: Assign Gaussians to oriented part regions, optimize appearance and geometry, and jointly enforce coherence and adjacency constraints.
assumptions: An articulated part structure represented by oriented bounding boxes is available.
limitations: The abstract does not specify how part boxes are obtained or the supported articulation range.

setup.summary: Evaluates articulated-object reconstruction quality and part geometry.

evidence.excerpt: Our approach leverages oriented bounding boxes of object parts to enforce two key structural properties.

bibliography.abstract: 4DHumanDiff directly generates text-conditioned dynamic human assets in 4D Gaussian space.

scope.rationale: The generated asset is an explicitly time-varying 4D Gaussian representation.

method.problem: Video-first text-to-4D pipelines are expensive and can produce incomplete or view-inconsistent human geometry.
method.solution: Train a diffusion model directly over structured 4D Gaussian assets with temporal attention and rendering regularization.

components.name: 3D U-Net
components.role: Generates the structured Gaussian asset directly from text conditioning.

components.name: Temporal attention
components.role: Models motion while preserving temporal coherence across the generated asset.

components.name: 4D interpolation
components.role: Smooths motion at inference without an additional trained interpolation model.

algorithm_steps: Encode the text condition, denoise a structured 4DGS asset with temporal attention, apply 2D regularization during training, and interpolate motion at inference.
assumptions: Training uses a large paired text-to-4DGS corpus.
limitations: Dataset access, exact training hardware, and detailed failure cases require full-source review.

setup.summary: Evaluates text-to-dynamic-human generation for temporal and multi-view consistency and inference speed.

methodology.summary: Compares consistency and generation time against video-first 4D generation pipelines.

evidence.excerpt: We present 4DHumanDiff, a diffusion framework that directly generates dynamic humans represented by 4D Gaussian Splatting.

bibliography.abstract: We propose Temporally and Spatially Ordered Gaussians (TSOG), a format for efficient representation of 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) content. TSOG extends the Spatially Ordered Gaussians (SOG) framework to the temporal domain by introducing a timeline attribute and temporal parameterization of geometry and appearance attributes. Similar to SOG, TSOG is a lossy format that assigns each Gaussian a unique index and encodes attribute values as index-aligned image data. TSOG is model-agnostic, extensible, and compatible with both discrete and continuous 4DGS representations. Evaluation using a PLYs sequence and FreeTimeGS as baselines, serving as simplistic and state-of-the-art 4DGS representations respectively, shows file size reductions exceeding 90%, with PSNR differences ranging between -0.42 and +0.85 dB. These results demonstrate substantial file size savings with minimal quality degradation, enabling efficient representation, storage, and delivery of dynamic scenes for next-generation 4D content.

datasets.name: SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 Volumetric Video Challenge compression-track dataset
datasets.split: Two provided scenes; first 100 frames per scene for the PLY-sequence experiment and all 300 frames per scene for the FreeTimeGS experiment.

datasets.name: Neural 3D Video
datasets.split: Five selected scenes excluding Flame Salmon; first 20 frames per scene for the PLY-sequence experiment and first 150 trained frames for the FreeTimeGS experiment.

evidence.excerpt: \title{TSOG: A format for Temporally and Spatially Ordered Gaussians}
\name{Shady Gmira, Evangelos Alexiou, Emmanouil Potetsianakis, Emmanuel Thomas}%\thanks{The authors intention is to make publicly available relevant source code.}}
Extending the PLY format with method-specific attributes hinders interoperability, whereas using sequences of PLY files (one per frame) results in excessive storage overhead and poor scalability.

Our contributions are: (i) we define the TSOG file format as a flexible extension of SOG with native temporal support; (ii) we experimentally evaluate TSOG in terms of file size and rendering quality; and (iii) we demonstrate the TSOG representation format by integrating it into PlayCanvas, highlighting its potential for wide deployment.

The TSOG file format retains the core SOG principle of a lossy design by quantizing and storing per-Gaussian parameters as index-aligned image data.
TSOG extends it by introducing a temporal dimension through the timeline attribute and temporal parameterization of geometry and appearance attributes, enabling its application to both discrete and continuous 4DGS representations.

The timeline attribute comprises temporal parameters that specify the lifespan of every Gaussian within or relative to the scene's timeline, which serves as a common time axis.
This lifespan is shared across the Gaussian's geometry and appearance attributes and defines the domain of their temporal parameterization.

The temporal parameters are chosen from one of the following three options: (1) \textit{Frame id}: Specifies the frame index in which this Gaussian is active. The \textit{fps} may be additionally signalled to specify corresponding time instances.

(3) \textit{Center} and \textit{scale}: \textit{Center} indicates the peak visibility time, and \textit{scale} represents the extent of a Gaussian's lifespan around the peak. The \textit{scene length} may be included to specify the duration of the scene (e.g., in sec). The first two options are more suitable for discrete 4DGS representations, while the last is better for continuous 4DGS representations.

Static attributes are stored in SOG images (i.e., defined by SOG).
Dynamic attributes are split between SOG images and newly introduced TSOG images.
For dynamic attributes modelled using polynomial temporal parameterization, base values (i.e., constant 0th-order coefficients) corresponding to the \textit{frame id}, \textit{start} or \textit{center} of a Gaussian's timeline are stored in SOG images.
Their higher-order coefficients describing their temporal evolution are stored in TSOG images specified under the \texttt{temporal} structure.

The TSOG file format preserves the original SOG~\cite{sog_2026} mapping for static attributes and base values of dynamic attributes without modification (i.e., SOG images).
Such attribute values are stored exactly as in SOG~\cite{sog_2026}, using the same spatial reordering, index alignment, channel layout, normalization, quantization, and metadata structure.
As a result, existing SOG decoding pipelines can process these images unaltered.

We evaluate the proposed TSOG file format in two complementary experiments using two datasets:
the dataset released for the compression track of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 Volumetric Video challenge~\cite{vvc2025siggraph} (VV), and the Neural 3D~\cite{neural_3d} dataset excluding Flame Salmon.

The source 4DGS contents are generated by training corresponding dynamic scene representations.
For the VV dataset, the 2 provided scenes were already trained using FreeTimeGS~\cite{wang_freetimegs:_2025}.
For the Neural 3D dataset, due to the lack of a public implementation of FreeTimeGS~\cite{wang_freetimegs:_2025},
each of the 5 selected scenes is trained using FreeTimeGS\-Vanilla~\cite{ftgs_vanilla} at half resolution with a target of 5~million Gaussians at SH3.

Then, for each experiment, a distinct baseline is created and used.
In the first experiment, a sequence of PLY files serves as the baseline for the most common discrete 4DGS representation.
In this case, we evaluate the trained model at every discrete time instance (frame) and save the resulting 3D Gaussians as an independent PLY file per frame.
In the second experiment, FreeTimeGS~\cite{wang_freetimegs:_2025} serves as the baseline for an advanced continuous 4DGS representation with temporal parameterization.

In each experiment, PSNR and SSIM are computed between images rendered from the baseline and the corresponding TSOG representation.
All reported metrics are computed on half-resolution rendered images.
All evaluations are performed using a single desktop RTX 4090.

For the VV dataset, we use the first 100 frames of each scene, whereas for the Neural 3D dataset, we use the first 20 frames of each scene.
This frame limit is imposed by the underlying WebP library used during TSOG encoding, which cannot handle images larger than roughly 25\,million pixels.

In this experiment, FreeTimeGS represents the baseline, with 4D Gaussians parameterized by continuous temporal attributes.
To convert FreeTimeGS content in the TSOG file format, the base values of position attributes are stored as static attributes.

Higher-order coefficients describing the linear evolution of position values are represented by per-Gaussian velocity vectors, and stored as a dynamic attribute in the temporal means image, specified under the \texttt{temporal} structure. The timeline attribute is configured with \texttt{type} set to 2, mapping the \textit{center} and \textit{scale} to the mean and standard deviation values used in FreeTimeGS's exponential parameterization of a Gaussian's temporal opacity.

For the VV~\cite{vvc2025siggraph} dataset, we use the full 300 frames of each scene, whereas for the Neural 3D dataset, we use the first 150 trained frames.
As part of this experiment, we evaluate 16-bit and 8-bit precisions for the temporal means.

We demonstrate the feasibility of TSOG representation format by integrating it into PlayCanvas~\cite{playcanvas_2026}, which is a widely used browser-based engine for real-time 3DGS visualization.
We extend PlayCanvas to parse and decode TSOG files, enabling dynamic playback of 4DGS content through index-aligned attribute images and temporal parameterizations.
Future work may extend TSOG to cover a broader set of temporal parameterization models and evaluate its performance under deployment-oriented conditions, such as streaming and web-based playback.

implementations.effect: Tests the TSOG format on a discrete sequence of per-frame Gaussian states.
implementations.name: Discrete PLY-sequence conversion
variants: TSOG with static attributes and a frame-ID timeline

implementations.effect: Tests the TSOG format on a continuous time-parameterized Gaussian representation.
implementations.name: Continuous FreeTimeGS conversion
variants: TSOG with temporal position coefficients and a center-scale timeline

methodology.summary: Compares discrete PLY-sequence and continuous FreeTimeGS baselines with their TSOG conversions; PSNR and SSIM are evaluated on half-resolution renders.

setup.summary: Evaluates two Volumetric Video Challenge scenes and five Neural 3D Video scenes excluding Flame Salmon; source content uses FreeTimeGS or FreeTimeGS-Vanilla.

lineage.rationale: Extends SOG's spatially reordered, index-aligned image mapping with per-Gaussian timelines and temporal-coefficient images for 4DGS content.

algorithm_steps: Assign every Gaussian a stable linear index shared across all attribute images.
Encode a per-Gaussian lifespan as frame ID, start-duration, or center-scale.
Store static attributes and dynamic base values in SOG images and higher-order temporal coefficients in TSOG images.
Decode matching pixels across SOG and TSOG images to recover synchronized time-varying attributes.
assumptions: Every Gaussian must have a timeline and all temporally parameterized attributes must map to the same pixel across their attribute images.
TSOG is a representation format and does not prescribe a 4DGS generation or rendering model.

components.name: Per-Gaussian timeline attribute
components.role: Defines each Gaussian's lifespan through frame-ID, start-duration, or center-scale temporal support.

components.name: Temporal attribute images
components.role: Store higher-order polynomial coefficients for dynamic geometry and appearance attributes while base values remain in SOG images.

components.name: Index-aligned SOG/TSOG mapping
components.role: Keeps each Gaussian at the same pixel coordinate across attribute images for synchronized decoding.

components.name: PlayCanvas TSOG decoder
components.role: Parses and decodes TSOG files for dynamic browser playback.

limitations: The WebP encoder's roughly 25-million-pixel image limit restricts the frame counts used in the discrete PLY-sequence evaluation.
Broader temporal parameterizations and deployment-oriented streaming and web playback remain future work.
method.problem: PLY-based 4DGS storage either requires method-specific temporal extensions or one PLY per frame, which harms interoperability, storage efficiency, and scalability.
pseudocode: for each Gaussian: assign one stable index shared across all attribute images
encode its lifespan as frame ID, start-duration, or center-scale in a timeline image
store static values and dynamic base coefficients in SOG images; store higher-order temporal coefficients in TSOG images
decode matching pixels across the SOG and TSOG images to recover synchronized time-varying Gaussian attributes
method.solution: TSOG is a lossy, model-agnostic 4DGS storage format that extends SOG with per-Gaussian timeline images and temporally parameterized attribute images while retaining per-index alignment.

scope.rationale: TSOG centrally defines a storage and delivery representation for 4D Gaussian Splatting content, including a per-Gaussian timeline and temporal parameterization, rather than merely evaluating or consuming 4DGS outputs.

bibliography.abstract: AdaAnchor4D adapts anchor-based spatiotemporal Gaussian deformation to heterogeneous monocular UAV scenes.

scope.rationale: The central representation deforms Gaussian anchors and their local primitives over time for dynamic reconstruction.

method.problem: Fixed plane-wise feature aggregation does not adapt well to spatially and temporally heterogeneous motion in monocular UAV scenes.
method.solution: Condition spatiotemporal feature aggregation on each anchor and time, decouple anchor motion from local Gaussian deformation, and warp queries according to anchor density.

components.name: ACFA
components.role: Aggregates shared spatiotemporal features with anchor-specific embeddings and temporal context.

components.name: DLGD
components.role: Separates anchor-state deformation from local Gaussian geometry deformation.

components.name: DACW
components.role: Adapts feature-query coordinates to non-uniform anchor distributions.

algorithm_steps: Aggregate anchor-conditioned temporal features, predict decoupled anchor and local deformation, then render the deformed Gaussians.
assumptions: Input is a monocular UAV video with usable camera information.
limitations: The official abstract does not yet document detailed optimization settings or failure modes.

setup.summary: Evaluated on UAV-Arc4D, VisDrone, and UAVDT for monocular UAV dynamic reconstruction.

methodology.summary: Compares rendering quality and real-time performance with representative dynamic Gaussian methods.

evidence.excerpt: We propose AdaAnchor4D, an adaptive anchor deformation framework for monocular UAV dynamic scene reconstruction.
